newsitem.title: POLAND: Policeman who killed Polish priest freed to work.
newsitem.headline: Policeman who killed Polish priest freed to work.

text.p: A Polish court has temporarily freed a former communist security policeman jailed for the 1984 murder of Catholic priest Jerzy Popieluszko, to let him earn money for his family, a court official said on Monday.

Grzegorz Piotrowski, a former captain of the now-defunct SB security police, will be free to work for six months before returning to serve out the rest of his term, said Boguslaw Moraczewski, head of a criminal department in the provincial court of Piotrkow Trybunalski, central Poland.

"He got a six-month break in the serving of his sentence and during these six months a company has guaranteed him work so he can help his family financially," Moraczewski told Reuters, adding that the family was in difficulties.

Piotrowski, 45, was sentenced to 25 years in 1985 for leading a squad that kidnapped, tortured and murdered Popieluszko, a supporter of the Solidarity union famed for his anti-communist sermons, in an action that shocked Poland's mainly Catholic population.
His sentence was later commuted to 15 years.

In 1994 he was granted parole after serving nearly 10 years of the term but an appeal by the Justice Minister against the ruling was upheld by the Supreme Court, because of the great cruelty of the premeditated killing.
Moraczewski said Piotrowski would have to go back behind bars on July 29 and had previously returned punctually to prison from earlier temporary releases during his sentence.
Three other security policemen involved in Popieluszko's killing were convicted in 1985 but have since been released.
